depth_justification: Structured and on-topic with mostly-correct GDPR citations (Art. 5(1)/(2), 6(1), 15-21, 9) and names Wav2Vec, but it is a templated one-dimension-per-turn march through P1, ignores the developer's repeated answer, leans on 'EU AI Act Art. 50' as a catch-all, and crucially never nails this kiosk's defining risks (voice emotion-recognition as a prohibited/high-risk AI-Act practice, MDR medical-device status, validity of waiting-room consent, false-positive clinical harm, front-desk confidentiality).
actionability_justification: Produces the requested severity-grouped report, but most mitigations are directional ('implement a retention policy', 'establish a legal basis', 'implement robust encryption and access controls', 'establish governance frameworks') rather than concrete recipes, with only a few near-specific items (explicit consent vs legitimate interest, delete-my-data button, portability options).
salient_examples: Repeated boilerplate: 'if the system processes biometric data... it may trigger additional obligations under the EU AI Act and GDPR Art. 9 [GDPR Art. 9]' without developing the emotion-recognition prohibition
Every turn ends 'Would you like to explore the next dimension, [P1.Dx]?' -- a fixed checklist march that ignores the user's 'Wav2Vec + classifier head' answer
Mitigation: 'Implement robust encryption, access controls, and data protection measures. GDPR Art. 30' -- directional, no specifics
Report is almost entirely P1 (purpose/legal basis/rights/retention/security); bias, human oversight, and clinical-harm risks largely absent
